title: Regional surge buffer and cost tranching forecast - private VPC capacity
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet lays out a pragmatic methodology for sizing private/VPC GPU fleet capacity with a regional surge buffer and a multi-tranche procurement plan to smooth capital spend and minimize cold-start risk. Intended audience: infra leads, SRE, procurement, and solutions engineering.

High-level goals:
- Meet 99th-percentile request throughput targets with 95% utilization target on steady-state boxes.
- Maintain a regional surge buffer to absorb traffic spikes and cross-region failover (target: 30% surge capacity at peak).
- Keep hot spare/replacement inventory for node failures (N+1 at per-rack level).
- Provide tranche plan: immediate, 6-month, 12-month purchases to adapt to model/quant improvements.

Assumptions (configurable variables):
- Model profile: medium-context chat (max seq 2048), average generation length 80 tokens.
- Average effective tokens/sec per GPU (H100 80GB, mixed-precision, optimized kernels): 420 tokens/sec for streaming chat workload.
- Request tokens per request (avg): 200 tokens (prompt+response).
- Target steady-state GPU utilization: 0.95 * sustainable throughput (we keep a safety multiplier in calculations).
- Surge factor: 1.30 (30% headroom for spikes).
- Availability target: 99.95% per region; require spare capacity for maintenance + rapid failover.
- Server density: 4x H100 GPUs per host. Rack density: 42U, two 1U redundant PSUs per host, 10 racks per pod typical.
- GPU cost estimate (purchase, 2026 list): H100 80GB = $35,000; A100 80GB = $22,000; Host (4-GPU chassis incl. CPU, NICs, storage, rails) = $45,000. Networking & power per rack budget = $25,000. Shipping/customs and integration multiplier = 1.12.

Input table (example demand forecast):
Region | Peak concurrent requests per sec (RPS) | Avg tokens/request | Tokens/sec demand | GPUs (raw) | GPUs with surge | GPUs after 4-per-server packing | Hosts required | Hosts with N+1 spare (5% host spare) | Estimated hardware CAPEX (USD)
NA-East | 1,250 | 200 | 250,000 | 250,000 / 420 = 595.2 -> 596 | 596 * 1.30 = 774.8 -> 775 | ceil(775 / 4) = 194 servers (776 GPUs) | +5% spare -> 204 hosts | hosts*host_cost*multiplier = 204 * 45,000 * 1.12 = $10,305,600
EU-Central | 720 | 200 | 144,000 | 144,000 / 420 = 342.9 -> 343 | 343 * 1.30 = 445.9 -> 446 | ceil(446 / 4) = 112 servers (448 GPUs) | +5% spare -> 118 hosts | 118 * 45,000 * 1.12 = $5,942,400
APAC-SG | 380 | 200 | 76,000 | 76,000 / 420 = 181.0 -> 181 | 181 * 1.30 = 235.3 -> 236 | ceil(236 / 4) = 59 servers (236 GPUs) | +5% spare -> 62 hosts | 62 * 45,000 * 1.12 = $3,126,000
Total (example) | | | 470,000 tokens/sec | GPUs raw ~1,121 | GPUs with surge ~1,457 | 1,520 GPUs packed into 380 hosts | hosts with spare 384 | Total CAPEX approx $19,374,000

Notes on the math and rounding policy:
- Tokens/sec demand = RPS * avg_tokens/request.
- GPU throughput taken from benchmark envelope; always include validation runs for your specific model (use internal eval harness).
- Surge buffer applied to GPUs (post raw calc), then pack into 4-GPU hosts. Rounding always rounds up at each stage to avoid under-provisioning.
- Host spare calculated at host-level (5% typical) to cover maintenance and immediate failover. For higher criticality customers use 10%.

Redundancy and failover configuration recommendations:
- Cross-region failover: maintain at least 20% of client-serving capacity in a secondary region or allow degraded modes (lower beam search size / shorter context) to reduce required capacity during full failover.
- Canaries and warm standby: keep a 2-rack warm-standby pool for canary testing and fast rollback.
- Maintenance windows: schedule rolling updates per-pod with 2-hour windows; ensure N+1 is available per rack to avoid capacity loss during patching.

Procurement tranching strategy (cost tranching):
- Tranche 0 (now, 0-3 months): Acquire 40% of estimated needed hosts to satisfy near-term demand and short-term growth; prioritize fastest-delivery SKUs (H100) and keep 20% of these purchasable as reserved spares.
- Tranche 1 (6 months): Acquire additional 35% to reach 75% of steady-state capability; evaluate actual token/sec realized; consider adding A100 fallbacks if H100 supply constrained.
- Tranche 2 (12 months): Final 25% with improved/next-gen GPUs or upgraded NICs; reserve budget for refresh or retrofitting with improved kernels/quantization that reduce GPU counts.
- Financial smoothing: spread payments to match revenue recognition (if customer prepaid reserved capacity) and hedge foreign-exchange by purchasing in local currency regions.

Bill-of-materials (BOM) snapshot (example for NA-East final target):
- GPUs: 776x H100 80GB (procure 800 including RMA spares)
- Hosts: 204 x 4-GPU chassis (plus 10 chassis spares)
- Racks: pod layout 10 racks per pod, 3 pods = 30 racks (include 2 spare racks for future expansion)
- Switches: 2x 100Gb leaf per rack redundant, 6x spine 400Gb — vendor quote required; budget line: $900,000 for network on pod scale
- Power: PDUs and feeders per rack, budgeted $25k/rack; for 30 racks = $750,000
- Cooling & layout: data center uplift estimates vary; plan 10% of hardware CAPEX as uplift baseline.

Operational considerations and runbook pointers:
- Monitoring: expose token/sec per-GPU, queue length per-host, response tail latency (p99.9). Alert thresholds: available GPUs drops below planned spare threshold; sustained utilization > 98% for > 10 minutes.
- Autoscaling rules: in private deployments autoscaling should be conservative; prefer queue-depth scaling and preemptive warm-up of reserved hosts.
- Firmware/driver matrix: pin a validated CUDA/CuDNN/driver image per-pod and record in the cluster manifest; test kernel-level changes in a single rack canary.

Risks and mitigations:
- Supply variability: maintain a two-vendor acquisition plan and allow A100 as temporary fallback tier with automatic routing policies that prefer H100 for latency-sensitive flows.
- Model efficiency improvements: if quantization or distillation reduces token/sec demand by > 20%, slow tranche 2 procurement to avoid over-buying.
- Power/cooling constraints: validate per-data-center power budget early; re-scope rack density if PDU limits force lower GPU-per-host counts.

Open questions (action items):
- Confirm region-specific customs and lead times with procurement (action: Miguel).
- Run internal benchmark for our prod model at 2048 context to confirm tokens/sec assumptions (action: Evelyn).
- Obtain vendor switch quotes for full pod networking (action: Rajiv).
- Decision on spare policy: host-level 5% vs 10% for top-tier customers (action: product).

Appendix: quick example formula snippets for the spreadsheet implementation (columns in a Google Sheet):
- tokens/sec = B2 * C2  (B2 RPS, C2 tokens/request)
- gpus_raw = ceil(tokens/sec / GPU_throughput)
- gpus_with_surge = ceil(gpus_raw * surge_factor)
- hosts_needed = ceil(gpus_with_surge / GPUs_per_host)
- hosts_with_spare = ceil(hosts_needed * (1 + host_spare_fraction))
- capex_region = hosts_with_spare * host_cost * procurement_multiplier + network_budget + rack_power_budget

This is a working draft: please comment inline with regional-specific numbers and attach actual vendor quotes in linked_artifacts.
